data.title: The Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques Quran, Sunnah Competition for West Africa Concludes in Mauritania with President in Attendance
data.content:
Nouakchott, November 19, 2026, SPA -- The second edition of the Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques Competition for the Memorization of the Holy Quran and the Prophetic Sunnah for West African countries concluded on Thursday in the Mauritanian capital, Nouakchott. Mauritanian President Mohamed Ould Cheikh El Ghazouani attended the closing ceremony, joined by senior officials and religious figures.
    The ceremony marked the end of four days of competitions involving 160 contestants from 16 African countries and concluded with the honoring of winners across the competition’s various categories.
    The event opened with a recitation from the Holy Quran, followed by official speeches highlighting the competition’s significance in serving the Holy Quran and the Sunnah, encouraging younger generations to memorize and master both, and strengthening fraternal ties between Saudi Arabia and Mauritania.
    Undersecretary of the Ministry of Islamic Affairs for Islamic Affairs Awad Al-Anzi delivered a speech on behalf of Minister of Islamic Affairs, Dawah and Guidance and General Supervisor of Local and International Quranic Competitions Sheikh Dr. Abdullatif Al Alsheikh. He said that serving the Holy Quran and Sunnah and supporting those who memorize them have been a firmly established commitment in Saudi Arabia since its founding.
    He noted that these efforts receive the care and support of Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud and the close follow-up of His Royal Highness Prince Mohammed bin Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, Crown Prince and Prime Minister.
    For his part, Mauritanian Minister of Islamic Affairs and Original Education Dr. Sid’Elhaje Ould Dah expressed his pleasure at the competition, saying: “We are filled with joy at this blessed gathering marking the conclusion of this major event.”
    He said the competition, which bears the name of the Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques, reflects the depth of fraternal relations between the two countries and that serving Islam remains a key foundation of their cooperation. He also praised Saudi Arabia’s leadership, government and people for their efforts to serve Islam and Muslims, as well as the work of the Ministry of Islamic Affairs, Dawah and Guidance in this regard.
    Attended by many television and radio outlets, the ceremony concluded with the honoring of winners across the Holy Quran and Sunnah categories and the distribution of cash prizes totaling SAR1.14 million.
    The event was marked by an atmosphere of joy and pride at this international Quranic gathering. The winners later posed for commemorative photographs with the Mauritanian president, senior officials and other participants.
    -- SPA
